incidents.victim: US, Taiwan, Japan, Poland — critical infrastructure
incidents.vector: Chinese government-linked contractor enabled state actors using the Microscan vulnerability scanner, IoT botnets, and the FishHub spearphishing tool to gain persistent access via living-off-the-land techniques and VPN tunneling
incidents.impact: Confirmed victims include a South Carolina power company, Taiwanese gas and power utilities, 20+ Taiwanese universities, and airports in Japan and Poland; FBI and DOJ seized Microscan and FishHub tools on Oct 8 in a second disruption of Integrity Tech operations, but the underlying actor group remains active

incidents.victim: Ukrainian transportation, manufacturing, and energy sectors
incidents.vector: Evolving MatchBoil downloader and MatchWok backdoor delivered via phishing; operators continuously modify malware and delivery methods to evade detection
incidents.impact: Ongoing espionage and sabotage-preparation operations against Ukrainian critical infrastructure; campaign active since 2023 with escalating activity through 2026 alongside conventional military operations

incidents.victim: South Korean banks
incidents.vector: ARTEX agentic AI pentesting tool autonomously identified vulnerabilities, crafted exploits, and exfiltrated data from financial institution systems — the first confirmed use of large-language-model-driven autonomous attack tooling in a banking breach
incidents.impact: Loan inquiry and mobile banking systems compromised; customer data and financial records exfiltrated; represents a significant escalation in AI-enabled offensive capabilities against financial services

incidents.victim: International business and government travelers at hotel networks globally
incidents.vector: DNS and HTTP traffic manipulation at hospitality networks redirects guests to device code phishing pages or fake software update sites that deploy credential-harvesting malware on their devices
incidents.impact: Unknown volume of high-value government, diplomatic, and business travelers compromised; campaign designed to intercept credentials and communications during international travel

incidents.victim: Taiwan academic and policy research organizations
incidents.vector: AI-generated academic event lures impersonating institutions, combined with real-time Google adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) phishing to bypass multi-factor authentication and capture session tokens
incidents.impact: Credentials and session tokens harvested from Taiwan research and policy professionals; scope of data theft under investigation

incidents.victim: Yoido Full Gospel Church and SaRang Church (South Korea)
incidents.vector: Web shell deployed on internet-facing servers in one intrusion; a second intrusion used leaked passwords and application vulnerabilities to access SAP business management systems and reset user credentials; attackers used AI tools for vulnerability analysis and data extraction
incidents.impact: 47 GB+ of data stolen including personal information, financial records, HR files, and internal communications for approximately 940,000 members across both churches; attack infrastructure linked to an earlier breach of a US Christian content platform

incidents.victim: Domain registrars for .gh (Ghana), .sl (Sierra Leone), and .as (American Samoa) TLDs
incidents.vector: Registrar-level compromise of three country-code TLD operators, enabling DNS manipulation for hosted domains and fraudulent TLS certificate issuance
incidents.impact: Invalid TLS certificates obtained for affected domains; Google Chrome added them to its revocation blocklist; local government and Google-hosted sites affected; potential for phishing and malware redirection before certificates were revoked

incidents.victim: FBI personnel portal and Jeppesen ForeFlight (Boeing navigation subsidiary)
incidents.vector: Mass exploitation of Oracle PeopleSoft zero-day CVE-2026-35273 to extract HR databases from government and commercial portals; active campaign June–September 2026
incidents.impact: 5,000+ FBI employee records exposed including unit assignments, clandestine operations classifications, and medical/psychiatric records; Jeppesen ForeFlight extorted; gang leader Rey (Jordan) detained, Dutch member Pepijn van der Stap arrested

incidents.victim: Software developers and cloud engineering teams globally
incidents.vector: Malicious packages planted across npm, PyPI, Go, and Rust package registries using Web3 blockchain infrastructure as command-and-control to exfiltrate cloud IAM tokens and CI/CD pipeline credentials from developer workstations
incidents.impact: Compromised the Axios npm package maintainer account; cloud access credentials stolen from organizations globally enabling follow-on infrastructure compromise; campaigns PolinRider and ChainDrop remain active

incidents.victim: Organizations running open-source AI services (LiteLLM, Ollama, Gitea, Gotenberg)
incidents.vector: PoeLLM malware encodes its command-and-control address inside keywords extracted from an innocuous-looking poem on GitHub, bypassing network monitoring; exploits a critical Ivanti Sentry vulnerability to infect servers hosting AI inference services
incidents.impact: 3,400+ servers compromised since April 2026; botnet used for cryptomining and scanning; compromised AI servers could be abused to exfiltrate prompts, steal API keys, or inject malicious model responses; botnet continues to grow by converting victims into new attack nodes

incidents.victim: Organizations running unpatched Atlassian Jira, Confluence, and Bitbucket
incidents.vector: Directory traversal via URL sanitization bypass (double-colon :: substitution) in Atlassian products allows unauthenticated attackers to read arbitrary files within the application directory, including configuration files containing credentials
incidents.impact: Active exploitation scanning from DigitalOcean infrastructure detected beginning Oct 7; patch released Oct 5; exposure window for unpatched systems includes web.xml and other configuration files that may contain credentials

incidents.victim: Organizations with internet-facing Fortinet FortiGate SSL VPN devices globally
incidents.vector: Active exploitation of internet-facing Fortinet FortiGate SSL VPN devices to harvest credentials; stolen hashes cracked offline using GPU acceleration; access packages sold to ransomware affiliates as initial foothold
incidents.impact: 86,644+ devices compromised across 194 countries; stolen VPN credentials resold to ransomware operators; some victims may be actively locked out of their own VPN infrastructure

incidents.victim: Iraqi telecommunications, aviation, and energy sectors
incidents.vector: Spearphishing via fake Dubai Airports recruitment lures delivers ShelbyLoader V2 through malicious .csproj file hijacking; GitHub repositories used as command-and-control infrastructure
incidents.impact: Persistent covert access established across Iraqi critical infrastructure beginning March 2026; long-term espionage collection ongoing in telecom, aviation, and energy sectors

incidents.victim: ASOS (British online fashion retailer)
incidents.vector: Attackers impersonated a trusted contact to dupe an employee into granting account access; employee credentials were then used to access third-party platforms, with attackers claiming to have breached ASOS's Snowflake cloud data environment
incidents.impact: Customer names and contact details accessed; unauthorized push notifications sent to the customer base causing ASOS shares to fall 10%+; payment card data and passwords not believed affected; group Xuanye Group claimed responsibility but had no prior track record

incidents.victim: Organizations using Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway globally
incidents.attacker: Unknown — likely financially motivated initial access brokers
incidents.vector: Two unpatched remote code execution zero-days (CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772) actively exploited since August 2026 to deploy persistent web shells on NetScaler ADC and Gateway appliances; no vendor patch available
incidents.impact: 50,277 potentially vulnerable NetScaler instances identified globally; web shells deployed for persistent access; compromised appliances sold as initial access or used for further network penetration by ransomware operators

incidents.victim: Government and policy organizations in Taiwan, India, Philippines, and Cambodia
incidents.vector: Deployment of previously undocumented 'Antino' backdoor targeting government and policy networks across Southeast Asia; delivery method under investigation
incidents.impact: Persistent covert access established in government networks across four countries; sensitive policy and diplomatic communications at risk; campaign assessed as ongoing

incidents.victim: Users of AI productivity tools seeking custom AI assistants
incidents.vector: Malicious custom AI chatbot interfaces impersonating legitimate tools use the ClickFix social engineering technique to trick users into executing commands that install Remote Access Trojans on their workstations
incidents.impact: RATs deployed on victim endpoints across multiple sectors; enables credential theft, data exfiltration, and ransomware staging; campaign targets users seeking AI productivity tools, broadening the attack surface beyond traditional phishing lures

incidents.victim: US Department of Defense — Defense Manpower Data Center (DMDC)
incidents.vector: Misconfigured file-sharing system left accessible online without authentication controls for approximately nine months (October 2025 to July 2026); unauthorized parties accessed exposed data during the window
incidents.impact: Personal data of 2.8 million living and 294,000 deceased US military personnel exposed, including names, military service information, and Social Security numbers

incidents.victim: Air Traffic and Navigation Services (ATNS), South Africa
incidents.vector: Ransomware deployed against ATNS operational technology network hosting weather-related services for air traffic controllers; possible insider collaboration is under investigation
incidents.impact: Attack stopped before disrupting flight operations; agency manages 6% of global airspace; weather data services for air traffic control disrupted; potential insider threat under investigation

incidents.victim: Bitget (Singapore-based cryptocurrency exchange)
incidents.vector: Attackers compromised one of three hot wallet layers used for customer transaction liquidity on the Bitget exchange, extracting cryptocurrency in a targeted hot wallet attack
incidents.impact: $350 million in cryptocurrency stolen; largest single crypto-exchange theft of 2026; investigation ongoing with no group claiming responsibility

incidents.victim: Arizona Supreme Court system
incidents.vector: Phishing email clicked by a court employee on September 24 gave attackers access; they accessed and copied backup files from the court's Fines/Fees and Restitution Enforcement (FARE) program and Foster Care Review Board systems before the IT team shut down the network
incidents.impact: 1.3 million people's data stolen including 30 years of SSNs and court case numbers; 150,000+ foster care reports compromised including records on 8,000 children currently in care; no ransomware, no ransom demanded

incidents.victim: Fideuram — Intesa Sanpaolo Private Banking (Italy)
incidents.vector: Fraudsters used AI voice cloning to impersonate the Intesa Sanpaolo CEO in messages and phone calls to the Fideuram chairman, obtaining authorization for fraudulent wire transfers to accounts in China and Hong Kong
incidents.impact: €95 million ($108M) transferred fraudulently; approximately €36 million remains unrecovered; first major documented case of AI voice impersonation used to defeat CEO-level transaction authorization controls at a major European bank
